headline: A slow-moving, very wet cold front crosses LA County between about 9 AM and noon Thursday with downpours of an inch an hour or more, a Flood Watch for nearly everywhere, and gusty south winds, before cool, dry weather takes over Friday and Saturday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain arrived in LA County before dawn Thursday, and the front itself has slowed down: it should reach Ventura County around 7–10 AM and sweep through LA County, including Glendale and Burbank, from about 9 AM to noon. It has been producing rain at more than an inch an hour (prompting several flash flood warnings farther north), and similar rates are likely as it passes, with storm totals of 1–3 inches for the coast and foothills and 2–5 inches on south-facing mountain slopes; a Flood Watch covers all areas except the Antelope Valley, running through Thursday afternoon for LA County. There is a 20% chance of a thunderstorm with the front and a very small chance (5% or less) of a weak tornado, best in the LA Basin later this morning, plus south winds of 35–50 mph under Wind Advisories that expire between 5 and 9 AM depending on the area. Highs only reach the mid 60s, a few showers may follow the front, and it should be dry by evening; 3–6 inches of snow may fall mostly above 7,000 feet near the end of the storm, too high to cause much trouble.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday turns dry, blustery and cool behind the storm, with fast northwest winds aloft and highs only in the low to mid 60s. A small area of high pressure brings a sunny Saturday, but highs rise just a degree or two and stay 4–8 degrees below normal.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A minor disturbance brings a 20–30% chance of rain Sunday, with any amounts under two tenths of an inch, and computer models keep trending weaker; highs stay in the mid 60s. Monday is dry and mostly sunny and still 4–8 degrees below normal, and weak land-to-sea (offshore) flow Tuesday warms things 2–3 degrees into the mid to upper 60s without much wind. The next storm could arrive Tuesday night or Wednesday, likely bringing rain to the Central Coast but only a 30–40% chance south of Point Conception, including LA County, with at most about a half inch; models still disagree, and Thanksgiving Day looks dry for now.

coast: Dangerous beach conditions continue into Friday, peaking Thursday, with High Surf Advisories for all beaches: large surf brings very dangerous rip currents and hazardous jetties. Minor to moderate coastal flooding is possible, especially at Thursday morning's high tide, with seawater over low-lying beaches, walkways and parking lots and significant beach erosion; a Coastal Flood Advisory runs until 10 AM Thursday for the Central Coast, where pier damage, flooded roads and possibly structures, and large breaking waves at Morro Bay Harbor (less so Ventura Harbor) are possible, with waves at or over the base of the Pismo and Cayucos piers. Offshore, gales are likely north of Point Sal and possible locally elsewhere, with Gale Warnings until 3–9 AM Thursday, Small Craft Advisories into Friday, and a chance of thunderstorms over the water; winds turn northwest behind the front, conditions improve Friday and turn fairly mild Saturday, and a weak front Sunday into Monday should have little impact. Extremely high, likely record-breaking tides arrive Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day), and with more swells increasingly likely they will probably cause at least widespread moderate coastal flooding on all coasts, possibly significant if a larger swell lines up with the tides; a stronger ocean storm around Thanksgiving is also possible.
watch_for: Downpours and street or freeway flooding as the front crosses LA County about 9 AM to noon Thursday, with a 20% thunderstorm chance and a small tornado risk
Whether the Tuesday night–Wednesday storm reaches LA County (30–40% chance) ahead of Thanksgiving
Record-high tides Thanksgiving week combined with new swells, raising the risk of widespread coastal flooding
confidence: Forecasters are confident in heavy rain with Thursday's front though timing has shifted later, confident in dry weather Friday through Monday, and have low confidence in the Tuesday night–Wednesday storm because computer models disagree.
